content.value_statement: Production errors are difficult to resolve without consistent telemetry and actionable alerts. This skill creates structured plans for tracking, grouping, reporting, and recovering from failures.
actual_capabilities: Assess existing error handling, logging frameworks, monitoring coverage, and common failure patterns.
Plan integrations with error tracking services and custom event reporting endpoints.
Design structured logs with severity levels, metadata, redaction, rotation, and production transports.
Define alert rules, error grouping, deduplication, performance metrics, and recovery strategies.
Outline real-time dashboards for error rates, affected users, trends, recent events, and active alerts.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not deploy or operate monitoring services.
Generated configurations require testing against the selected platform, runtime, and data protection rules.
Examples cover common patterns and may require adaptation for unsupported languages or vendors.
The skill cannot diagnose production incidents without relevant logs, traces, code, and system context.

use_cases.title: Establish Error Tracking
use_cases.description: Create an implementation plan for event capture, sensitive-data redaction, service integration, and deployment validation.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Alerts
use_cases.description: Design grouped alerts with thresholds, escalation routes, rate limits, and actionable diagnostic context.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability
use_cases.description: Define shared logging fields, dashboard metrics, recovery policies, and troubleshooting documentation across services.

prompt_templates.title: Review Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this application error handling approach. Identify missing capture points, weak context, and the three highest-priority improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment of an existing application

prompt_templates.title: Plan Service Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an error tracking integration plan for [runtime] using [service]. Include configuration, redaction, sampling, release tracking, and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for a selected monitoring service

prompt_templates.title: Design Alerts and Grouping
prompt_templates.prompt: Design alert and grouping rules for [system]. Address fingerprints, severity, thresholds, escalation, duplicate suppression, and recovery notifications.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Observability Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design production error observability for [architecture]. Cover collection, structured logs, privacy controls, performance impact, dashboards, resilience, and rollout verification.

output_examples.input: Assess error monitoring for a Node.js API that only writes console errors.
output_examples.output: The assessment identifies missing structured context, centralized reporting, request correlation, and alert ownership. It prioritizes capture middleware, redaction, and deployment verification.

output_examples.input: Create alert rules for a payment service with repeated timeout errors.
output_examples.output: The plan groups timeouts by dependency and operation, defines rate and impact thresholds, limits duplicate notifications, and includes recovery alerts.

output_examples.input: Plan an error dashboard for several production services.
output_examples.output: The dashboard includes error rate, affected users, top groups, service trends, recent events, active alerts, and mean recovery time.

best_practices: Provide the runtime, deployment model, monitoring vendor, traffic profile, and data sensitivity before requesting implementation guidance.
Redact credentials and personal data before sharing logs or sending events to any monitoring service.
Test capture, grouping, alert delivery, performance overhead, and recovery behavior in a controlled environment before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not send complete request bodies, credentials, or personal data to error tracking systems.
Do not alert on every event without grouping, thresholds, ownership, and escalation rules.
Do not deploy generated examples without adapting dependencies, security controls, and failure handling to the target environment.

faq.question: Does this skill support a specific monitoring vendor?
faq.answer: It provides vendor-neutral guidance and examples for common services, including Sentry-style and custom reporting integrations.

faq.question: Can it analyze my existing error handling?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant code, logging configuration, architecture details, and expected failure scenarios.

faq.question: Does it automatically access production logs?
faq.answer: No. It only uses context and files supplied through the active coding environment.

faq.question: How does it protect sensitive information?
faq.answer: It recommends explicit redaction, restricted event context, controlled destinations, and validation against applicable privacy requirements.

faq.question: Can it create alerting and dashboard plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define metrics, grouping, thresholds, escalation paths, real-time views, and validation steps.

faq.question: Is generated configuration ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Review and test every configuration against your runtime, vendor, security controls, traffic, and operational procedures.
